question: How are NYC crashes distributed across the days of the week, 2013 to 2025?

options.grouping: Day of week derived from crash_date, Monday through Sunday, pooled across 2013-2025
options.reason: A pooled count gives the direct overall distribution of reported crash records across weekdays during the full requested period.
options.answer: Among the 2,132,218 in-range crash records, Friday had the most reported crashes (338,800) and Sunday the fewest (257,544).
options.interpretation: Each row is one police-reported crash, and its weekday is derived from crash_date; the bars count records from 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31 pooled together. Friday is the largest category at 338,800 crashes and Sunday the smallest at 257,544, giving the aggregate weekday distribution but not its year-to-year variation or exposure-adjusted risk. The check found 2,132,218 in-range rows, no missing crash dates or derived weekdays, and no default/sentinel dates, so all in-range rows were retained; 100,545 records before 2013 and 36,424 after 2025 were excluded. Observed dates span January 1 to December 31 in every year, though those endpoints alone do not prove complete reporting within each year.

options.metric: Within-year share of police-reported crashes for each day of the week
options.denominator: All in-scope crashes with a valid crash_date in the same calendar year
options.grouping: Calendar year and day of week derived from crash_date, Monday through Sunday
options.chart_type: Year-by-weekday line chart of annual shares
options.reason: Year-specific shares reveal whether the weekday mix changes over time without letting variation in total annual crash counts dominate the comparison.
options.answer: Friday had the largest within-year share in every year, while its share declined from 16.25% in 2013 to 15.53% in 2025 and Sunday's rose from 11.85% to 13.09%.
options.interpretation: Each row is one police-reported crash; weekday is derived from crash_date, and each line plots a weekday's share of that same calendar year's in-range reported crashes for 2013-2025. Friday has the largest share in all 13 years, while from 2013 to 2025 Friday's share moves from 16.25% to 15.53% and Sunday's from 11.85% to 13.09%; this within-year denominator shows mix changes rather than absolute annual volume. It does not show crash risk per amount of travel or other exposure. The check found 2,132,218 in-range rows, no missing crash dates, years, or weekdays and no default/sentinel dates, so all in-range rows were kept; 100,545 records before 2013 and 36,424 after 2025 were excluded, and each year's observed dates span January 1 to December 31, although that does not establish reporting completeness within the year.

answer:
- Pooled across 2013–2025, Friday had the most reported crashes (338,800) and Sunday the fewest (257,544).
- Friday had the largest within-year share in every year; its share declined from 16.25% in 2013 to 15.53% in 2025, while Sunday’s rose from 11.85% to 13.09%.
